summary.text: The Galois group of a certain type of field extension is a symmetry group describing how the extension builds on its base field.
Each element of the group is a transformation of the larger field that leaves every element of the base field fixed.
Through the fundamental theorem of Galois theory, group tools can attack field problems, such as describing the solutions to quintic polynomials.

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Évariste Galois, who first discovered them

facts.label: What its elements do
facts.value: Transformations that leave the base field fixed

facts.label: Finite abelian groups
facts.value: Each one is a Galois group of some cyclotomic subfield

facts.label: Complex over reals
facts.value: A cyclic group of order 2, from complex conjugation

items.prompt: What kind of object is the Galois group of a field extension?

options.label: A list of the coefficients of the polynomial involved
A count of how many roots the polynomial has
A symmetry group showing how the extension sits over its base field
A table of the prime numbers inside the field

items.explain: It is a symmetry group that characterizes how the extension extends the base field.

items.prompt: A transformation of the bigger field is a candidate for the Galois group only if it does what to the smaller base field?

options.label: Leaves each element of the base field unchanged
Swaps every element of the base field with another
Doubles every element of the base field
Sends the base field onto the larger field

items.explain: Every element of the Galois group leaves each element of the base field fixed.

items.prompt: The complex numbers a + b i are extended from the reals. The only symmetries of C that keep every real number fixed are doing nothing and swapping a + b i for a − b i. What size is this symmetry group?

options.label: Trivial, with a single element
Infinite, with one for each real number
Four elements, one per sign choice
Two elements, identity and conjugation

items.explain: Gal(C / R) is the cyclic group of order 2: the identity and complex conjugation, which fixes every real number.

items.prompt: Why do mathematicians bother connecting fields to groups at all?

options.label: It makes every field finite and easy to list
It lets group tools be used on problems about fields
It replaces polynomials with simple numbers
It avoids ever needing the base field

items.explain: The connection lets group-theoretic tools be used on field problems, such as describing the solutions of quintic polynomials.

items.prompt: Someone claims only a few special finite abelian groups can ever show up as Galois groups. What does the Kronecker–Weber theorem say about subfields of cyclotomic extensions?

options.label: Only cyclic ones of prime order appear
Only the trivial group appears
Any finite abelian group can be found
Only groups with exactly two elements appear

items.explain: By the Kronecker–Weber theorem, any finite abelian group arises as the Galois group of some subfield of a cyclotomic field extension.

items.prompt: Whose name is attached to this group, and why?

options.label: Abel, who proved the quintic cannot be solved
Galois, who first discovered these groups
Liouville, who first published the theory
Kronecker, who linked it to cyclotomic fields

items.explain: The study is named in honor of Évariste Galois, who first discovered Galois groups.
